def set_fact(
    fluents, fluent_name, args, holder, round_number,
    narration=None, visibility="agent_only", event_type="fact_initiated",
):
    """General-purpose fluent write: terminate any open record for this
    exact (fluent_name, args) pair, then open a new one. assign_role() is
    the role-shaped special case of this (see below); use this directly for
    non-role facts — an obligation, a sanction, a status a norm wants
    tracked — where `holder` may be an individual agent_id or the sentinel
    "community" for a fact that isn't about one specific agent.

    `narration` is optional, already in-world-phrased plain language
    (the same convention phases/*.py's memory_writes() already uses for its
    `text` field) describing this fact for whoever it's visible to. A
    record with no narration renders nowhere — it's plumbing only (this is
    how plain role_fluent records, like the "fisher" role every agent
    holds, stay invisible to the notice renderer without needing a
    migration). `visibility` is `"public"` (surfaced to every agent) or
    `"agent_only"` (surfaced only when `holder` matches the requesting
    agent) — only meaningful when `narration` is set. Default to
    `"public"` for anything a community norm would plausibly want logged or
    monitored (this project's own adopted norms consistently call for
    public ledgers/monitors); use `"agent_only"` for something between one
    agent and the mechanism, like an individual warning.

    Whenever `narration` is set, the same text also reaches the memory
    layer automatically (see `fact_memory_events()` below) — `event_type`
    picks which of `engine/memory/write.py`'s `IMPORTANCE_BY_EVENT_TYPE`
    entries it's logged under; the generic `"fact_initiated"` default is
    fine unless a more specific existing type applies (e.g.
    `"graduated_sanction_applied"` for a real sanction).
    """
    for record in fluents:
        if (
            record["fluent"] == fluent_name
            and record["args"] == args
            and record["terminated_round"] is None
        ):
            record["terminated_round"] = round_number
    record = {
        "fluent": fluent_name,
        "args": args,
        "holder": holder,
        "initiated_round": round_number,
        "terminated_round": None,
    }
    if narration is not None:
        record["narration"] = narration
        record["visibility"] = visibility
        record["event_type"] = event_type
    fluents.append(record)
    return fluents


def end_fact(
    fluents, fluent_name, args, round_number,
    narration=None, visibility=None, event_type="fact_ended",
):
    """Terminate the open record for (fluent_name, args), if any, without
    opening a replacement — e.g. a ban that's been served in full. Pass
    `narration` to describe the closing event itself (e.g. "Your ban has
    been lifted.") — same rules as `set_fact()`: reaches prompt (for
    exactly the round it closes, via `visible_facts()`) and memory
    automatically. `visibility` defaults to the record's own opening
    `visibility` if not given; only meaningful when `narration` is set."""
    for record in fluents:
        if (
            record["fluent"] == fluent_name
            and record["args"] == args
            and record["terminated_round"] is None
        ):
            record["terminated_round"] = round_number
            if narration is not None:
                record["end_narration"] = narration
                record["end_visibility"] = (
                    visibility if visibility is not None else record.get("visibility", "agent_only")
                )
                record["end_event_type"] = event_type
    return fluents


def _visible_to(agent_id, holder, visibility):
    return visibility == "public" or holder == agent_id


def visible_facts(fluents, agent_id, round_number):
    """Every fluent record with something narrated for right now and
    visible to agent_id — either public, or held by agent_id itself. Two
    cases: a currently-holdsAt record's opening `narration` (visible for
    as long as the fact stays open), and a record that closed exactly this
    round, surfaced via its `end_narration` for that one round only (the
    two are mutually exclusive per record: a record can't be both
    currently-open and closed-this-round). Used by the engine's prompt
    renderer to build an agent's "what's currently true" section; never
    interprets a raw value itself, only surfaces narration the mechanism
    that wrote the fact already authored."""
    results = []
    for record in fluents:
        if (
            record.get("narration")
            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("visibility"))
            and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
            and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
        ):
            results.append(record)
        elif (
            record.get("terminated_round") == round_number
            and record.get("end_narration")
            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility"))
        ):
            results.append({**record, "narration": record["end_narration"]})
    return results


def fact_memory_events(fluents, round_number):
    """Memory-episode specs for every fact newly opened or newly closed
    this exact round that carries narration — pure, no I/O (mirrors the
    shape `phases/*.py`'s `memory_writes()` already returns:
    `{event_type, text, agent_id, group_id}`). The caller
    (`engine/simulate.py`) turns these into actual `write_episode()` calls,
    once per round after all of that round's phases have run — not once
    per phase, since a fact set by an early phase would otherwise still
    read as "newly opened" to a later phase's own call and get logged
    twice."""
    events = []
    for record in fluents:
        if record.get("initiated_round") == round_number and record.get("narration"):
            events.append(_memory_spec(
                record["holder"], record.get("visibility", "agent_only"),
                record.get("event_type", "fact_initiated"), record["narration"],
            ))
        if record.get("terminated_round") == round_number and record.get("end_narration"):
            events.append(_memory_spec(
                record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility", "agent_only"),
                record.get("end_event_type", "fact_ended"), record["end_narration"],
            ))
    return events


def _memory_spec(holder, visibility, event_type, text):
    group_id = "community" if visibility == "public" else holder
    agent_id = None if holder == "community" else holder
    return {"event_type": event_type, "text": text, "agent_id": agent_id, "group_id": group_id}

1. Policy: The lake reserve must never fall below 60 kg; each fisher may take at most 2 kg per trip (including the 1 kg needed for survival); any fish beyond 2 kg must be returned immediately; if the reserve ever drops below 60 kg, fishing is suspended until the reserve recovers to 60 kg or more; violations result in a temporary fishing ban.
   In practice: At the start of each fishing day, the community checks the current reserve via the shared ledger. If reserve ≥60 kg, each fisher records catch on the ledger and is limited to 2 kg; excess fish must be returned right away. After the day's catches, the ledger updates the reserve; if reserve <60 kg, all fishers stop fishing for that day and resume only when the reserve ≥60 kg. Any fisher who fails to return excess fish receives a 2‑week fishing ban. The community meets monthly to review reserve levels and adjust the cap if needed.

2. Policy: Each fisher may keep up to 6 kg per trip; excess catch is deposited into a communal reserve, and the total daily catch is capped at 15 % of the lake’s current stock.
   In practice: Before each trip the community records the lake’s stock and sets the 15 % cap. After the trip, each fisher reports their catch. If total catch exceeds the cap, all catch is reduced proportionally until the cap is met. Any fisher who caught less than 1 kg receives the remainder from the reserve so everyone gets at least 1 kg. The reserve is replenished by voluntary contributions from those who exceed the 6 kg allowance. Failure to report or to adhere to the cap results in forfeiture of that day’s share for that fisher. The rule is reviewed monthly to adjust the cap if the lake’s stock changes significantly.

3. Policy: Each fisher may keep up to 15 kg per trip; any catch below 5 kg is topped up from a communal reserve; any catch above 15 kg is returned to that reserve.
   In practice: At the end of each trip, a fisher reports their catch. If the catch is less than or equal to 5 kg, the community supplies enough fish from the reserve to bring the fisher’s total up to 5 kg. If the catch exceeds 15 kg, the excess fish is returned to the reserve. The reserve is replenished by a small fixed fraction of each fisher’s catch (for example, 1 kg per 10 kg caught) to keep it stocked. If a fisher attempts to keep more than 15 kg without returning the excess, or fails to report their catch, they must forfeit their entire haul for that trip and incur a community penalty (e.g., a small fee deducted from the next trip’s payout).

4. Policy: Each fisher may keep up to 35 kg per trip; any catch beyond 35 kg must be deposited into a community reserve. Fishers who catch less than 3 kg in a trip may withdraw up to 5 kg from the reserve to make up their shortfall.
   In practice: After each trip, every fisher records their catch on a communal ledger. If the catch is ≤35 kg, the fisher keeps it all; if it exceeds 35 kg, the excess goes into the reserve. If a fisher’s catch is <3 kg, they may claim a withdrawal from the reserve, limited to 5 kg. Withdrawals are logged and replenished by any fisher who catches >35 kg, by contributing the equivalent weight to the reserve. Non‑compliance (e.g., not reporting catch or misusing reserve) results in a 10 kg deduction from the fisher’s next trip quota.

5. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 12 kg per trip, must leave at least 12 % of their haul in the lake, and the lake must hold at least 45 kg after all fishing; any catch above the 12 kg cap is donated to a shared reserve that is redistributed if lake stocks fall below 45 kg.
   In practice: Each fisher records their haul in a communal ledger each day. If their haul exceeds 12 kg, they keep 12 kg and donate the excess to the reserve. After all fishing in a round, the lake’s remaining stock is checked; if it is below 45 kg, the reserve is split evenly among all fishers. Failure to record or to donate excess results in a 1 kg credit penalty in the next round. If the lake’s stock is already below 45 kg before a round begins, no fishing is allowed until the reserve can be used to raise the stock to 45 kg.

6. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 12% of the lake’s current stock per trip, must deposit 0.5 kg per trip into a shared reserve, and no fisher may exceed 65% of the lake’s initial stock over the season; the lake must retain at least 35% of its pre‑fishing stock after every round.
   In practice: Before each trip, fishers check current lake stock via community gauge. They set a personal limit of 12% of that stock for the trip and collect the agreed 0.5 kg reserve. They record catch in a communal ledger; if a fisher exceeds the limit or fails to deposit, the excess is confiscated and a 1 kg fine is levied. The reserve is used for emergency sustenance when stock falls below 35% of the original 100 kg. Community leaders enforce compliance by reviewing ledger weekly.

7. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 6% of the lake’s current biomass per day, must keep at least 1 kg for themselves, and deposit any catch above that into a communal restocking fund; the lake must retain at least 30% of its pre‑fishing biomass after all trips.
   In practice: Each fishing day, a fisher calculates 6% of the lake’s current biomass (as agreed by the community) and is allowed to take that amount; they keep at least 1 kg for personal use, and any catch beyond the 6% limit or beyond the 1 kg must be deposited into the communal restocking fund. After all fishing in a season, the community verifies that the lake’s remaining biomass is at least 30% of the initial pre‑fishing level; if a fisher exceeds the 6% quota, they pay the excess to the fund, and if the 30% threshold is not met, a temporary fishing ban is imposed.

1: # Reads: state/config.json (effort caps), state/fluents.json (role holders),
2: # engine/physics.py (fixed catch/regrowth/consumption rates).
3: # Writes: state/runtime.json (today's catch, payoff, deaths), state/fluents.json (deaths).
4: 
5: from mechanisms.effort import effort_cap
6: from mechanisms.stock_check import available_stock
7: from mechanisms.roles import set_fact, end_fact
8: from engine.physics import (
9:     catch_from_effort,
10:     apply_regrowth,
11:     apply_consumption,
12:     is_dead,
13:     alive_agent_ids,
14:     CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
15: )
16: from engine.llm_agents import call_fisher_agent
17: from engine.phase_base import Phase
18: 
19: 
20: class HarvestPhase(Phase):
21:     name = "harvest"
22: 
23:     def prompt_fields(self, state, agent_id):
24:         config = state["config"]
25:         fluents = state["fluents"]
26:         runtime = state["runtime"]
27:         round_number = state["round_number"]
28:         cap = effort_cap(agent_id, config, fluents, runtime)
29:         cap_line = (
30:             f" You currently have an agreed limit of {cap:.0f}kg for this trip."
31:             if cap is not None
32:             else ""
33:         )
34:         return {
35:             "stock_kg": available_stock(runtime),
36:             "carrying_capacity_kg": CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
37:             "cap_line": cap_line,
38:             "stock_trend": self._stock_trend(runtime, config, round_number),
39:         }
40: 
41:     def _stock_trend(self, runtime, config, round_number):
42:         """A short recent-history readout of surveyed stock levels, oldest
43:         to most recent — lets a fisher notice for themselves whether the
44:         lake has been recovering or shrinking, the same way Gupta et al.'s
45:         CPRAgent prompt gives a rolling `resource_history` window rather
46:         than stating the regrowth rate outright (never named or quantified
47:         here — no "growth_rate", no formula, just what a fisher would
48:         actually observe trip to trip). Window size matches
49:         render_history()'s own `history_window_rounds` so both readouts
50:         cover the same span of rounds."""
51:         window = config.get("history_window_rounds", 5)
52:         past_harvests = [
53:             r for r in runtime["rounds"]
54:             if r["phase"] == "harvest" and r["round"] < round_number
55:         ][-window:]
56:         if not past_harvests:
57:             return "This is the first count anyone's taken — no earlier surveys to compare against."
58:         levels = ", ".join(f"{r['stock_kg_after_regrowth']:.0f}kg" for r in past_harvests)
59:         return f"The last few counts, oldest to most recent, were: {levels}."
60: 
61:     def run(self, state):
62:         config = state["config"]
63:         fluents = state["fluents"]
64:         runtime = state["runtime"]
65:         agents = state["agents"]
66:         round_number = state["round_number"]
67: 
68:         runtime.setdefault("payoff", {})
69:         runtime.setdefault("dead_agents", [])
70: 
71:         stock_before = available_stock(runtime)
72:         results = {}
73:         cumulative_kept = 0.0

from mechanisms.effort import effort_cap
from mechanisms.stock_check import available_stock
from mechanisms.roles import set_fact, end_fact
from engine.physics import (
    catch_from_effort,
    apply_regrowth,
    apply_consumption,
    is_dead,
    alive_agent_ids,
    CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
)
from engine.llm_agents import call_fisher_agent
from engine.phase_base import Phase


class HarvestPhase(Phase):
    name = "harvest"

    def prompt_fields(self, state, agent_id):
        config = state["config"]
        fluents = state["fluents"]
        runtime = state["runtime"]
        round_number = state["round_number"]
        cap = effort_cap(agent_id, config, fluents, runtime)
        cap_line = (
            f" You currently have an agreed limit of {cap:.0f}kg for this trip."
            if cap is not None
            else ""
        )
        return {
            "stock_kg": available_stock(runtime),
            "carrying_capacity_kg": CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
            "cap_line": cap_line,
            "stock_trend": self._stock_trend(runtime, config, round_number),
        }

    def _stock_trend(self, runtime, config, round_number):
        """A short recent-history readout of surveyed stock levels, oldest
        to most recent — lets a fisher notice for themselves whether the
        lake has been recovering or shrinking, the same way Gupta et al.'s
        CPRAgent prompt gives a rolling `resource_history` window rather
        than stating the regrowth rate outright (never named or quantified
        here — no "growth_rate", no formula, just what a fisher would
        actually observe trip to trip). Window size matches
        render_history()'s own `history_window_rounds` so both readouts
        cover the same span of rounds."""
        window = config.get("history_window_rounds", 5)
        past_harvests = [
            r for r in runtime["rounds"]
            if r["phase"] == "harvest" and r["round"] < round_number
        ][-window:]
        if not past_harvests:
            return "This is the first count anyone's taken — no earlier surveys to compare against."
        levels = ", ".join(f"{r['stock_kg_after_regrowth']:.0f}kg" for r in past_harvests)
        return f"The last few counts, oldest to most recent, were: {levels}."

    def run(self, state):
        config = state["config"]
        fluents = state["fluents"]
        runtime = state["runtime"]
        agents = state["agents"]
        round_number = state["round_number"]

        runtime.setdefault("payoff", {})
        runtime.setdefault("dead_agents", [])

        stock_before = available_stock(runtime)
        results = {}
        cumulative_kept = 0.0
        for agent_id in alive_agent_ids(agents, runtime):
            cap = effort_cap(agent_id, config, fluents, runtime)
            response = call_fisher_agent(
                agent_id, round_number, "harvest", **self.prompt_fields(state, agent_id)
            )
            effort = min(1.0, max(0.0, float(response["effort"])))
            harvested = catch_from_effort(effort, stock_before)
            # Enforce norm: Fisher may keep up to 8 kg per trip; excess goes to communal reserve.
            # Determine the maximum keepable amount, respecting any effort cap.
            max_keep = 8.0
            if cap is not None:
                max_keep = min(max_keep, cap)
            # Amount the fisher actually keeps before possible withdrawal
            kept = min(harvested, max_keep)
            # Enforce total daily catch cap: 20 % of lake stock across all fishers.
            max_total = 0.20 * stock_before
            remaining = max_total - cumulative_kept
            if remaining <= 0:
                kept = 0.0
            else:
                kept = min(kept, remaining)
            cumulative_kept += kept
            # Excess goes to reserve
            reserve_added = harvested - kept
            # Initialize communal reserve if not present
            runtime.setdefault("communal_reserve_kg", 0.0)
            # Apply reserve cap: cannot exceed 20 % of the lake’s current stock (stock_before)
            max_reserve = 0.20 * stock_before
            new_reserve_total = runtime["communal_reserve_kg"] + reserve_added
            runtime["communal_reserve_kg"] = min(new_reserve_total, max_reserve)
            # If fisher kept less than 1 kg, allow withdrawal up to the shortfall from reserve.
            if kept < 1.0:
                shortfall = 1.0 - kept
                withdraw = min(shortfall, runtime["communal_reserve_kg"])
                kept += withdraw
                runtime["communal_reserve_kg"] -= withdraw
            # Handle missing report: if response lacked 'effort' field, reduce share by 1 kg (or to zero) and add to reserve.
            if "effort" not in response:
                reduction = min(1.0, kept)
                kept -= reduction
                # Add reduced amount back to reserve respecting cap
                runtime["communal_reserve_kg"] = min(runtime["communal_reserve_kg"] + reduction, max_reserve)
            # Use the final kept amount as harvested for consumption calculations.
            harvested = kept

            new_payoff = apply_consumption(runtime["payoff"].get(agent_id, 0.0), harvested)
            runtime["payoff"][agent_id] = new_payoff

            results[agent_id] = {
                "effort": effort,
                "harvested_kg": harvested,
                "reasoning": response.get("reasoning", ""),
            }

            if is_dead(new_payoff):
                runtime["dead_agents"].append(agent_id)
                name = agents[agent_id]["name"]
                set_fact(
                    fluents, "dead", [agent_id], agent_id, round_number,
                    narration=f"{name} has died — they hadn't been catching enough fish to survive.",
                    visibility="public",
                )
                end_fact(fluents, "fisher", [agent_id], round_number)

        # No proportional rationing here — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(),
        # which subtracts each agent's independently-computed catch (all against the
        # same pre-harvest stock) directly, letting the stock go negative if
        # oversubscribed. The existing collapse check below (stock <= 0) is this
        # project's equivalent of their stop-the-simulation condition.
        stock_after_harvest = stock_before - sum(r["harvested_kg"] for r in results.values())
        stock_after_regrowth = apply_regrowth(stock_after_harvest)

        round_record = {
            "round": round_number,
            "phase": "harvest",
            "stock_kg_before": stock_before,
            "agents": {
                agent_id: {
                    "effort": result["effort"],
                    "harvested_kg": result["harvested_kg"],
                    "reasoning": result["reasoning"],
                }
                for agent_id, result in results.items()
            },
            "stock_kg_after_harvest": stock_after_harvest,
            "stock_kg_after_regrowth": stock_after_regrowth,
        }

        runtime["round"] = round_number
        runtime["stock_kg"] = stock_after_regrowth
        runtime["rounds"].append(round_record)
        return round_record

1. Policy: The lake reserve must never fall below 60 kg; each fisher may take at most 2 kg per trip (including the 1 kg needed for survival); any fish beyond 2 kg must be returned immediately; if the reserve ever drops below 60 kg, all fishing is suspended until the reserve recovers to 60 kg or more; violations result in a temporary fishing ban.
   In practice: Before each trip, a fisher must consult the community monitor to confirm the lake reserve is ≥60 kg. If so, the fisher may catch up to 2 kg; any fish above 2 kg is immediately returned and the excess logged in the communal ledger. After every trip, the fisher records the exact catch in the ledger and signs it. The lake reserve is measured by the monitor every month, and if it falls below 60 kg, the community declares a fishing suspension until the reserve recovers. A fisher who fails to return excess fish or record the catch is subject to a one‑trip ban. The monitor also ensures that no fishing occurs when the reserve is below 60 kg.

2. Policy: Each fisher may keep up to 5 kg per trip; any excess goes to a communal reserve; the total daily catch is capped at 12 % of the lake’s current stock.
   In practice: All fishers record their catch on a shared ledger each day. If a fisher takes more than 5 kg, the surplus is automatically moved to the reserve. If the combined daily catch exceeds 12 % of the lake’s stock, the excess is also moved to the reserve. Fishers who catch less than 1 kg receive an equal share from the reserve to cover their minimal needs. Failure to record or to deposit excess results in a one‑trip suspension. A rotating committee of fishers manages the reserve and distributes aid.

3. Policy: Each fisher may keep up to 20kg per trip; any catch below 3kg is topped up by the communal reserve; any catch above 20kg is returned to that reserve.
   In practice: After each trip every fisher reports their catch to the community. The community tallies total catch and adds a 5% tax to the communal reserve. If a fisher's catch is under 3kg, the reserve supplies the shortfall; if it exceeds 20kg, the excess is returned to the reserve. If a fisher fails to report, they lose the right to fish for the following week. The lake stock is monitored weekly; if it falls below 30kg, fishing is suspended until the reserve reaches at least 50kg, at which point fishing resumes.

4. Policy: Each fisher may keep up to 30 kg per trip; any fish beyond 30 kg is deposited into a community reserve that can be withdrawn by fishers who catch less than 5 kg per trip to make up their shortfall.
   In practice: At the end of each trip every fisher records their catch and deposits any surplus beyond 30 kg into the reserve, verified by a rotating registrar chosen from the community. Fishers who catch under 5 kg can request up to 5 kg from the reserve, but only if they have not exceeded the 30‑kg cap in more than half of their recent trips. The reserve is logged daily; if it falls below 10 kg the community must vote to temporarily lower the 30‑kg cap to 25 kg for all fishers until the reserve is replenished. Non‑compliance (failing to deposit surplus or to report catch) results in loss of reserve access for that fisher until the issue is corrected.

5. Policy: Each fisher may take no more than 10 kg per trip, must leave at least 12 % of their haul in the lake, and the lake must hold at least 45 kg after all fishing; any catch above the 10 kg cap is added to a shared reserve that is redistributed if lake stocks fall below 45 kg.
   In practice: Every fisher records their haul in a communal ledger each day. The ledger tracks total daily catch, applies the 10 kg cap, and moves excess to the shared reserve. If the projected lake stock after today’s catch would dip below 45 kg, no further fishing is allowed until the reserve is used to bring the lake back above 45 kg. When the lake is above 45 kg again, the reserve is redistributed proportionally to those who need extra fish. Anyone who fails to record their haul or exceeds the 10 kg cap has the excess transferred to the reserve and receives a one‑day fishing ban for that day.

6. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 10% of the lake’s current stock per trip, deposit 1 kg per trip into a shared emergency reserve, no fisher may exceed 50% of the lake’s initial stock over the season, and the lake must retain at least 35% of its pre‑fishing stock after every round.
   In practice: Before each trip, the fisher records the lake’s current stock and calculates 10% of that as the maximum allowed catch. During the trip the fisher sets aside 1 kg into a communal reserve bin that is overseen by a rotating community steward. After each round, the reserve is counted, and if the lake’s remaining stock would fall below 35% of the original stock, all fishers must reduce their catches accordingly. If a fisher fails to deposit the 1 kg or exceeds the 10% limit, their catch for that round is forfeited, and they are temporarily banned from fishing until they pay back a 0.5 kg penalty or complete a community‑service hour. The reserve can be used to supply the minimum 1 kg of food to any fisher who cannot catch enough due to low fish density.

7. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 6% of the lake’s current biomass per day, must keep at least 1 kg for themselves, and deposit any excess into a communal restocking fund; the lake must retain at least 25% of its pre‑fishing biomass after all trips.
   In practice: Before each trip a fisher calculates 6% of the lake’s current biomass; that is the legal catch limit. They must retain at least 1 kg. If they catch more than 1 kg, the surplus goes into a communal restocking fund. All catches are logged in a shared ledger. If a fisher exceeds the 6% limit, they pay a penalty equal to the excess to the fund. At season’s end we sum the pre‑season biomass and verify the lake still holds at least 25% of that amount; if it falls short, fishing is halted until the lake recovers and any surplus caught must be returned to the lake or deposited.
